segments.name: The Two Mothers, the Two Schools

stops.name: South Bronx, the birth to Florence Spellman
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date and the borough; no source reviewed names a hospital, a street, or an attending physician, so the coordinate marks the Bronx generally and not a specific place
stops.campa: Florence Spellman is nineteen and unmarried when she gives birth in the Bronx to a son she names Lawrence Joseph. The father has already gone; the accounts that mention him at all give a first name and nothing further. No hospital, no address, no attending physician survives in the record, and the borough is the whole of what the biographies agree on. She keeps the boy nine months, through a winter and into a pneumonia that decides the rest of his life for him. Then she gives him away.
suggested_refs: Birth records of the Bronx, August 1944, unlocated in any published account
sources: Britannica Money, 'Larry Ellison'
EBSCO Research Starters, 'Larry Ellison'
Notable Biographies, 'Ellison, Larry'

stops.name: South Shore, Chicago, the child handed to the great-aunt
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the standard biographies date the transfer to his ninth month, after the pneumonia, but give no month and cite no document. The date here orders the segment only
stops.campa: Sick with pneumonia, the infant is handed to Florence's aunt and uncle, Lillian Spellman Ellison and Louis Ellison, who adopt him and raise him in a small apartment in South Shore, a lower-middle-class Jewish neighborhood on the south side of Chicago. He is about twelve when he learns that the woman raising him is not his mother. He goes to South Shore High School quick and argumentative, remembered as sharp in the subjects that hold him and entirely absent from the ones that do not.
suggested_refs: The South Shore apartment of Lillian and Louis Ellison, address unrecorded in published sources
sources: Britannica Money, 'Larry Ellison'
Notable Biographies, 'Ellison, Larry'

stops.name: Urbana-Champaign, the second year left unfinished
stops.date_confidence: attested for the enrollment and the departure without final examinations; the term of his leaving is not fixed in the sources, and the September date marks the start of the enrollment
stops.campa: He enters the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign on an understanding that belongs to his family rather than to him, that he is going to be a doctor. He is named science student of the year. In his second year Lillian dies, and he leaves without sitting his final examinations. He does not go back. He keeps the subject and drops the credential, and he will do the same thing again in Chicago four years later. That summer he is back in the South Shore apartment, saying almost nothing to Louis about any of it.
suggested_refs: University of Illinois science student of the year citation, early 1960s
sources: Academy of Achievement, 'Larry J. Ellison'
Britannica Money, 'Larry Ellison'

stops.name: Hyde Park, one term and the first machine
stops.date_confidence: attested as a single term in 1966; the sources give no month, and the January date orders the segment
stops.campa: He enrolls at the University of Chicago for a single term, physics and mathematics, and there meets a computer for the first time, its design and its programming. He does not finish this term either. He leaves Hyde Park with no transcript and with a skill that pays contract rates in a city full of mainframes, and the family is still angry about the medical school. Two universities have now had him and neither has issued him a degree. Before the term is out he has stopped pretending he means to graduate. He is twenty-one.
suggested_refs: The University of Chicago computation facilities of the mid-1960s
sources: Academy of Achievement, 'Larry J. Ellison'

segments.name: West, and the Machine at Ampex

stops.name: Berkeley, the drive west with a guitar
stops.date_confidence: traditional; Ellison's own account in the 2016 USC commencement address dates the drive to his twenty-first year and gives no month
stops.campa: He loads a car in Chicago and drives to California. In the Bay Area he takes contract programming wherever it pays, at Fireman's Fund, at Wells Fargo, at Amdahl, learning the machines by being handed them. The work pays a self-taught programmer better than a physics department pays a graduate student. He marries Adda Quinn, whom he met through an employment agency, and they live thinly on what the contracts bring. By his own later telling she leaves because he lacks ambition. She divorces him in 1974.
stops.quote: I was 21 years old when I dropped out of college, packed everything I owned, jeans, t-shirts, leather jacket, guitar, into my car, and drove from Chicago to Berkeley, California.
stops.quote_source: Larry Ellison, USC commencement address, 13 May 2016, transcript published by The Singju Post
suggested_refs: Contract programming work at Fireman's Fund, Wells Fargo and Amdahl, late 1960s
sources: Britannica Money, 'Larry Ellison'
Biography.com, 'Larry Ellison: From College Dropout to Billionaire Oracle Founder'

stops.name: Ampex, 401 Broadway, Redwood City, the two men he will need
stops.date_confidence: traditional; company histories place his Ampex years in the early to mid 1970s without a start date, and the January date orders the segment
stops.campa: At Ampex, a video and mass-storage company on Broadway in Redwood City, Ellison works alongside Bob Miner, a programmer who had come to the machines through Persian-language study, and Ed Oates. Miner is the engineer Ellison is not. Oates will make the third. Ampex at this moment is building a very large storage system for the Central Intelligence Agency's Office of Joint Computer Support, a machine to hold more data than any commercial customer of 1970 wants held. The internal designation for the work is ORACLE.
stops.quote: My family was still mad at me for not going to medical school, and now my wife was divorcing me because I lacked ambition.
stops.quote_source: Larry Ellison, USC commencement address, 13 May 2016, on the years before Oracle
suggested_refs: Ampex Corporation, 401 Broadway, Redwood City, and its CIA mass-storage work
sources: Business Insider, 'The CIA Made Larry Ellison A Billionaire'
Britannica Money, 'Larry Ellison'

stops.name: Redwood City, the acceptance report on Project ORACLE
stops.date_confidence: attested for the document, dated 1975. The declassified pages name Ampex and the Office of Joint Computer Support and do not name Ellison anywhere; his presence on or near the project rests on company histories and his own later telling, not on the CIA record. The January date orders the segment
stops.campa: The Agency's acceptance report on the Ampex system records serious failures moving data between disk and tape memory. The machine does not work as promised. Released through the CIA reading room decades afterward, the ORACLE files run to a handful of unglamorous procurement pages: specifications, complaints, a system that underperformed. Larry Ellison is not mentioned in them. What the pages establish is an Ampex contract and its failure. Who at Ampex was in the room when the word was chosen, and who carried it out of the building afterward, is not in the file and has never been documented anywhere else.
suggested_refs: CIA Reading Room, Project ORACLE files CIA-RDP83T00573R000500080009-3 and CIA-RDP83T00573R000500040011-4
sources: CIA Reading Room (FOIA), Project ORACLE memoranda
Business Insider, 'The CIA Made Larry Ellison A Billionaire'

stops.name: Santa Clara, Software Development Laboratories incorporated
stops.date_confidence: attested for the incorporation date and place. Some accounts give an early office at 20 Davis Drive, Belmont, which was the company's headquarters address in the following decade, not its 1977 premises
stops.campa: Ellison, Miner and Oates incorporate Software Development Laboratories with about two thousand dollars, of which Ellison puts up roughly twelve hundred. Miner is the technical architect. Ellison is thirty-two and is going to sell. The founding idea belongs to an IBM researcher: Edgar Codd published the relational model in 1970 and IBM's own System R team built SQL on top of it. IBM is in no hurry to ship a product that would undercut the database business it already has. The papers are filed at Santa Clara on 16 June 1977.

stops.name: Langley, the Agency buys the first copy
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. No contract, price or signing date has ever been made public; the claim rests entirely on Ellison's own repeated public statements. The coordinate is the customer's address, not an attested Ellison journey, and nothing in the released record places him at Langley
stops.campa: The young company's first paying customer, by Ellison's account given many times over the following decades, is the Central Intelligence Agency, buying a relational database for a project the founders have named after the Ampex contract they came from. No document confirming the sale has ever surfaced. What survives is the founder's telling, repeated at customer conferences until it set into the company's origin story, and on top of it a legend that the Agency owned the company. Nothing in any filing supports the legend.
stops.quote: The very first version was Oracle version 2. We knew no one would buy version 1. Low and behold the CIA was our first customer.
stops.quote_source: Larry Ellison, Oracle OpenWorld opening keynote, San Francisco, 28 September 2014, as printed by Business Insider, 29 September 2014
suggested_refs: Ellison's Oracle OpenWorld 2014 keynote account of the company's first customer
sources: Yahoo Finance / Business Insider, 'Larry Ellison Is A Billionaire Today Thanks To The CIA'

stops.name: Santa Clara, the version that never had a first
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of the release; the sources reviewed give no month, and the January date orders the segment
stops.campa: Renamed Relational Software, the company ships Oracle Version 2. There was no Version 1. The number is a sales decision, taken so that a buyer evaluating a two-year-old firm will believe he is looking at something already proven in the field. Around the same product grows the demonstration login a generation of database administrators will type without thinking: username SCOTT, password TIGER, after Bruce Scott, the first employee, and his daughter's cat. Scott's sample schema of employees and departments is still being taught forty years later.
stops.quote: There was no 'V1.' The 'V2' was a marketing ploy to create the illusion of a more mature product.
suggested_refs: The SCOTT/TIGER demonstration account and the EMP/DEPT sample schema
sources: Computer History Museum, 'Oracle Database'

stops.name: Belmont, 20 Davis Drive, the company address and the family
stops.date_confidence: attested for the Belmont headquarters, occupied through the 1980s until the 1989 move to Redwood Shores. The year orders the family events, whose dates the sources dispute: CNN gives the Boothe marriage as 1983 to 1987, Wikipedia as 1983 to 1986
stops.campa: The company, now Oracle Systems Corporation, works out of Belmont. Ellison has married twice more since Adda Quinn. Nancy Wheeler Jenkins gave up her interest in the young firm for five hundred dollars in their divorce. Barbara Boothe, an early Oracle employee, is his wife now; their son David is born this year and their daughter Megan in 1986. The marriage ends in 1986 or 1987, depending on which record is consulted. Neither child spends much of a childhood with him. Both will go into film.
suggested_refs: Oracle's Belmont headquarters at 20 Davis Drive, occupied until 1989
sources: Biography.com, 'Larry Ellison: From College Dropout to Billionaire Oracle Founder'

stops.name: Belmont, the shares listed one day before Microsoft's
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date, the exchange and the fifteen-dollar offer price. The first-day close is given as $20.75 in one account and $19.25 in another, so it is stated here as near twenty dollars rather than as a flat figure
stops.campa: Oracle goes public on the NASDAQ at fifteen dollars a share and closes the first day near twenty; one account of the close gives $20.75 and another $19.25. Microsoft lists the following morning. The two companies enter the public market within a day of each other and will spend the next twenty years telling customers that the other one is the danger. Ellison is forty-one and rich for the first time. Revenue is doubling annually. The sales force is paid on contracts signed, not on software delivered.
suggested_refs: Oracle's NASDAQ prospectus and first-day trading record, 12 March 1986
sources: Begin To Invest, 'March 12th - This Day in Stock Market History'

segments.name: Redwood Shores: the Restatement and the Wave

stops.name: Redwood Shores, the towers on the lagoon
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of the relocation; no month given in the sources reviewed
stops.campa: Oracle moves its headquarters to Redwood Shores, filled marshland on the bay with an artificial lagoon, where cylindrical towers of green glass will go up around the water. Ellison will run the company from here for three decades. Inside, the sales organization is pushed harder every quarter, and the number that matters is the count of contracts signed before the last day of the period. Within a year the auditors will take that number apart. From the freeway the buildings look like a bank of disk drives stood on end, green glass over standing brown water.
suggested_refs: Oracle world headquarters, 500 Oracle Parkway, Redwood Shores
sources: Fortune, 'Oracle CEO Larry Ellison on Texas, California, Hawaii'
Britannica Money, 'Larry Ellison'

stops.name: Redwood Shores, three quarters of a year restated
stops.date_confidence: attested for the restatement, the loss and the collapse in the share price, which ran across the second half of 1990; the September date orders the sequence. The fiscal year ended 31 May 1990 and three of its four quarters were restated, not a single quarter as several summaries have it
stops.campa: Oracle has reported record revenue of $970.8 million for the fiscal year. An internal audit finds that revenue has been booked on the signature of a contract rather than the delivery of the software. Three of the four quarters are restated, revenue cut to about $916 million and earnings from $117 million to roughly $80 million. Weeks later comes the first quarterly loss in the company's history, about $36 million. The stock falls from twenty-eight dollars to six and a quarter, and the shareholders sue Oracle and its auditor.
suggested_refs: In re Oracle Securities Litigation, 829 F. Supp. 1176 (N.D. Cal. 1993)
sources: Federal court record, In re Oracle Securities Litigation
Contemporaneous financial press on Oracle's fiscal 1990 restatement

stops.name: The North Shore, Oahu, the board in three pieces
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction on two counts. The date is contested: CNN dates the accident to Christmas Day 1991, bodysurfing in Hawaii, while a Forbes profile of 30 September 1998 places it in the previous autumn, 1997, and the bicycle crash in 1998. The beach is unnamed in every source checked, which describe only closed water, red flags and waves of twelve to fifteen feet; the North Shore coordinate is a guess and is flagged as one
stops.campa: The beach is closed and the flags are out. He goes in anyway, into twelve- to fifteen-foot surf, and the board comes apart in three pieces; a fragment drives into his neck and breaks a vertebra, and he punctures a lung. He is in his late forties and the company he restated a year earlier has only begun to recover. The sources cannot agree which year this happened. He recovers, and then, riding a bicycle during the recovery, shatters his left elbow.
suggested_refs: Forbes profile of 30 September 1998 describing the surfing accident and the bicycle crash
sources: Forbes, 'Larry Ellison' profile, 30 September 1998
CNN Fast Facts, 'Larry Ellison'
Academy of Achievement, 'Larry J. Ellison'

stops.name: San Francisco, the death of Bob Miner
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date, the age and the cause. Some accounts place the death at Woodside, which the memorial record does not support
stops.campa: Robert Nimrod Miner dies of pleural mesothelioma in San Francisco, two years after stepping back from the daily running of the company he co-founded and wrote the first working code for. He had been the engineer of the partnership, the one who built what Ellison sold. The product line from Version 2 through the Oracle7 release of 1992, which restored the company after the restatement, rests on architecture he set. The disease was diagnosed the year before. He is fifty-two.
suggested_refs: Obituary record for Robert Nimrod Miner, San Francisco, 11 November 1994
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bob Miner'
Find a Grave memorial 125595824
orafaq, Oracle corporate history

stops.name: Sacramento, the elbow and the building that follows it
stops.date_confidence: attested for the surgeries and for the naming; the Lawrence J. Ellison Ambulatory Care Center opened in 1998, and the earlier musculoskeletal research center gift dates from the years of his treatment
stops.campa: The shattered elbow takes four operations under the surgeon Murray Chapman at the University of California, Davis. Out of the gratitude comes money: first the Lawrence J. Ellison Musculoskeletal Research Center, then an ambulatory care center on the Sacramento campus carrying his name, opened in 1998. It is the first institution anywhere to bear his name. He arrived at Davis as a patient with a smashed arm and left it a donor, and the building is still there on the campus with the name over the entrance.
suggested_refs: Lawrence J. Ellison Ambulatory Care Center, UC Davis Health, Sacramento
sources: UC Davis Health, 'Philanthropic couple spearheads fundraising for Emergency and Surgical Services Pavilion'

segments.name: Sayonara, and the Friend at Apple

stops.name: Cupertino, 1 Infinite Loop, the seat kept for a friend
stops.date_confidence: attested for the 1997 appointment and for the resignation announced on 20 September 2002; the month of joining is given as August, when Jobs's return was formalized, and the sources do not fix a day
stops.campa: Steve Jobs comes back to Apple and Ellison joins its board. The two have been friends for years, walking the hills above Woodside. Ellison had floated in public the idea of financing a takeover to put Jobs back in charge, and dropped it when Jobs told him the return could be managed without buying the company. He sits on the board five years, through the founder's restoration and the first iMac. In September 2002 he resigns, citing his schedule. When he marries at Woodside the following year, Jobs takes the photographs.
suggested_refs: Apple Newsroom, 'Larry Ellison Resigns as Apple Director,' 20 September 2002
sources: Apple Newsroom, 'Larry Ellison Resigns as Apple Director'

stops.name: Sydney Harbour, Sayonara at the start line
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Sayonara, Ellison's eighty-two-foot maxi yacht, crosses the start of the Sydney to Hobart race on Boxing Day with a professional crew and every intention of taking line honours. A hundred and fifteen boats start. Ellison is aboard, fifty-four years old and three seasons into racing this boat hard. The forecast is bad and gets worse through the afternoon as the fleet clears the heads and turns south for Bass Strait. Behind them the harbour is still thick with spectator craft, as it is every year, boats full of people who will read about the rest of it in the papers.
suggested_refs: The 1998 Sydney to Hobart race fleet, 115 starters
sources: France 24, 'Fatal storm haunts Sydney-Hobart yacht race 20 years on'
Wired, 'Staying Afloat in Australia'

stops.name: Bass Strait, the depression that catches the fleet
stops.date_confidence: attested for the storm and the date; the coordinate is an approximate open-water position on the fleet's track and not a fixed landmark
stops.campa: A hurricane-force low forms over the strait and runs into the fleet. Sayonara, out in front, meets it first: seas the crew afterward put at sixty feet, wind past seventy knots, the boat falling off the backs of waves and men breaking ribs on the way down. Behind them boats roll, dismast and lose people over the side. Six sailors die. Fifty-five are lifted off by helicopter and five yachts are abandoned. Ellison, below with a crew that includes an America's Cup skipper, is told the hull may not hold.
suggested_refs: The 1998 Sydney to Hobart storm, six deaths, 55 rescued by helicopter
sources: The Register, 'Ellison looks back on the horrors of the Sydney/Hobart yacht race'

stops.name: Constitution Dock, Hobart, line honours at six minutes past eight
stops.date_confidence: attested; Sayonara took line honours at 08:06 on 29 December 1998, elapsed time two days nineteen hours and six minutes. Accounts giving 28 December are wrong against the race record
stops.campa: Sayonara comes in first, two days nineteen hours and six minutes out of Sydney, into a dock where nobody is celebrating. Of the hundred and fifteen boats that started, forty-four finish; five have been abandoned at sea and six men are dead. The crew is put ashore exhausted, into a harbour that has been taking mayday traffic for two days. He tells the story often in the years afterward, and it is the one part of his record he did not have to arrange. Ellison accepts the trophy and says he will never sail the race again. He does not.

sources: The Register, 'Ellison looks back on the horrors of the Sydney/Hobart yacht race'

stops.name: Washington, the investigators and the office trash
stops.date_confidence: attested for the episode and the year; the admission came in the summer of 2000, during the federal antitrust case against Microsoft, and the date orders the segment
stops.campa: Oracle admits it hired Investigative Group International to look into the organizations publicly defending Microsoft in the federal antitrust case. The investigators approached cleaning staff for the discarded paper of Microsoft-aligned advocacy groups. Ellison does not apologize. He holds a press conference to explain that the object was to show who had been paying the independent voices, and that a public service had been performed. Microsoft is under order at that moment to be broken in two. The press calls the episode Peeping Larry.
stops.quote: Some of the things our investigator did may have been unsavory. Certainly from a personal-hygiene point they were. I mean, garbage, yuck.
stops.quote_source: Larry Ellison, quoted in 'Peeping Larry,' Time, 2000
suggested_refs: Investigative Group International's Washington opposition research for Oracle, 2000
sources: Time, 'Peeping Larry,' 2000

stops.name: Washington, the card and the free software
stops.date_confidence: attested for the proposal, made publicly in the weeks after the September 11 attacks; the day is used to order the segment
stops.campa: Within weeks of the attacks Ellison proposes that the United States consolidate its federal databases and issue every citizen a national digital identity card, and offers Oracle's software to the government free of charge. The offer is not disinterested: the licences are free, the maintenance is not, and only one company sells databases at that scale. Civil liberties organizations answer at once. His argument is that the data already sits in a hundred incompatible places, that privacy is therefore already gone, and that what remains at issue is competence.
suggested_refs: Ellison's national identity card proposal, September and October 2001
sources: Contemporaneous national press coverage of Ellison's national-ID proposal, September-October 2001

stops.name: Woodside, the wedding in the samurai house
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date and the officiant; the exact parcel within Woodside is not independently confirmed and the coordinate marks the estate generally
stops.campa: He marries the novelist Melanie Craft on the estate he has built above Woodside, a compound modeled on a sixteenth-century samurai residence with a lake and hand-joined timber, the product of years of collecting Japanese architecture, gardens and armor. Congressman Tom Lantos, the only Holocaust survivor ever elected to the United States Congress, officiates. Steve Jobs takes the photographs. It is Ellison's fourth marriage, the guest list is short, and Lantos will take him to Israel four years later.
suggested_refs: The Woodside estate modeled on a sixteenth-century Japanese residence
sources: Contemporaneous society and business press coverage of the Ellison-Craft wedding, December 2003

stops.name: Redwood Shores, PeopleSoft taken after eighteen months
stops.date_confidence: attested for the agreement in December 2004 and for the price; the announcement day varies slightly across accounts
stops.campa: Oracle agrees to buy PeopleSoft for about $10.3 billion, ending an eighteen-month hostile campaign that PeopleSoft's board fought with a poison pill, a customer refund guarantee and a lawsuit. The United States Department of Justice sued to block the merger on antitrust grounds and lost at trial. Ellison keeps the software and cuts thousands of the people who wrote it. Siebel, BEA, Sun, NetSuite and Cerner follow over the next eighteen years, bought the same way.
suggested_refs: United States v. Oracle Corp., N.D. Cal. 2004, the failed antitrust challenge

stops.name: Harvard Yard, the pledge withdrawn
stops.date_confidence: attested for the pledge and its withdrawal, reported in June 2006 after Summers announced his resignation in February of that year
stops.campa: Ellison had pledged $115 million to Harvard for an institute to measure whether global health programs actually work, a project carried by the university's president, Lawrence Summers. Summers resigns under faculty pressure in February 2006. Ellison withdraws the pledge, unpaid, and the institute is never built. The money had never left his hands. The Crimson reports the withdrawal in June; Harvard says little. Whether the $115 million was ever promised to the university or only to Summers is a question neither party has answered on the record.
suggested_refs: The Harvard Crimson, 'Ellison Pulls Plug on $115M,' 30 June 2006

stops.name: Sderot, the community center with nothing over it
stops.date_confidence: attested for the visit and the pledge, reported in the Israeli press in August 2007; the day given is the date of publication
stops.campa: He travels to Israel with the foreign minister Tzipi Livni and with Tom Lantos, who married him at Woodside four years earlier. In Sderot, a town inside rocket range of Gaza, he is shown a community center with no reinforcement over the roof, and pledges half a million dollars to protect it. The Beverly Hills galas and the hardened data center under Jerusalem all come after this. He is sixty-three, and until this week his public life had almost nothing to do with Israel.

stops.name: Santa Clara, Sun Microsystems absorbed
stops.date_confidence: attested for the closing date and the price
stops.campa: Oracle closes its $7.4 billion purchase of Sun Microsystems and takes Java, Solaris, SPARC and MySQL. Ellison now owns the language a great deal of the world's enterprise software is written in, and sues Google over its use of the Java interfaces in Android; the Supreme Court will rule against Oracle on fair use in 2021. Sun's chief security officer, Whitfield Diffie, does not wait for the close. He leaves in November 2009 while the deal is pending, ending eighteen years there. Oracle is now a hardware company.

stops.name: Lana'i City, ninety-eight percent of an island
stops.date_confidence: attested for the purchase and for the reported price; the exact figure was never disclosed by either party
stops.campa: Ellison buys about ninety-eight percent of the Hawaiian island of Lana'i from Castle and Cooke for a price reported near three hundred million dollars. He gets the two resorts, most of the housing, the water utility, the airport services and the store. Some three thousand people live there, and their landlord, their employer and their water are now one man, operating through a company called Pulama Lana'i. He talks about a laboratory for sustainability, solar power, desalination. The island's arguments after 2012 are about water and rent.

stops.name: Redwood Shores, on the necessity of being watched
stops.date_confidence: attested for the interview and its broadcast date. Whether it was recorded at Oracle's headquarters or in a studio is not established, and the pin is his working base in this period
stops.campa: Two months after Edward Snowden's disclosures, with the surveillance argument at full volume, Ellison sits for CBS and calls the National Security Agency's bulk collection essential, naming the Boston Marathon bombing as what it exists to prevent. He is the only major technology chief executive that summer to defend the program without qualification. The instrument under discussion is the sort of database he has sold for thirty-six years. Asked when such a program would become objectionable, he names one condition, and the condition is not the collecting.
stops.quote: If the government used it to do political targeting. If the Democrats used it to go after Republicans. If the Republicans used it to go after Democrats.
stops.quote_source: Larry Ellison, CBS This Morning, 13 August 2013

stops.name: San Francisco, the Cup defended from eight races down
stops.date_confidence: attested for the final race date and the result; the two-point penalty was imposed by the international jury before the match began
stops.campa: Ellison's syndicate had taken the America's Cup at Valencia in 2010 after years of litigation with the defender, and brought it to San Francisco Bay. Oracle Team USA sails for the Golden Gate Yacht Club, is docked two points for illegal modifications to smaller test boats, and goes eight races down to New Zealand. Then it wins eight straight, on foiling catamarans doing forty knots inside the bay, and keeps the trophy nine to eight. Ellison was not found to have ordered the modifications.

stops.name: Redwood Shores, thirty-seven years as chief executive end
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Ellison steps down as chief executive after thirty-seven years and hands the job to Safra Catz and Mark Hurd as co-chief executives. He becomes executive chairman and chief technology officer, keeping the engineering and the board and giving away the operating meetings. The cloud business he is about to bet the company on does not yet exist at scale. Nobody at Redwood Shores calls it a retirement; the architecture decisions stay his.
